prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1151; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a collision at an intersection where the insured vehicle was turning left and was struck by an oncoming vehicle. The claimant reports neck pain and has not retained counsel.

Entry 2: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant describing the approach, the signal phase, and the moment of impact. The account is consistent with the initial report.

Entry 3: Reviewed photographs supplied by the claimant, which confirm the general position of the vehicles and several details of the damage. No independent witnesses have come forward to date.

Entry 4: Estimate of damage to the vehicle is mostly in line with the impact described, with the damage concentrated on the front and side areas expected for this type of collision. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 5: Police report and statements from other parties confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck strain. The reported injury fits the kind and force of the crash well. Medical records were requested and the claimant signed authorization for release.

Entry 7: Medical file shows treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant disclosed a small strain to the same area several years ago that healed fully, and that history has been noted.

Entry 8: Claimant later added a few small details to the account during a follow-up call, but the core description of events stayed the same as in the original statement.

Entry 9: Confirmed the driver involved lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy. File reviewed and remains open pending final medical summary.
